Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)
Referred Sections: CMM-609.4: Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) with Decompression (Indirect or Direct)

Required findings: The prior adjacent-level lumbar fusion was performed at least 6 months prior to the current request.
Criteria have been met in the applicable procedure-specific section (CMM-609.4 for fusion with decompression or CMM-609.5 for fusion without decompression).

Medical necessity indications.Guideline Category: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression (Indirect or Direct)
Required findings: The individual is a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.

Imaging findings include specific criteria for Actual Instability (e.g., degenerative spondylolisthesis with dynamic instability >3mm or Meyerding Grade II+; spondylolisthesis with spondylolysis with progression or Grade III+; post-operative instability from facet excision >50% bilateral or 75% single facet; pars fracture; or iatrogenic spondylolisthesis).

Imaging findings include specific criteria for Anticipated Iatrogenic Instability (e.g., facet excision >50% bilateral or 75% single facet; pars removal; decompression for Meyerding Grade I+ spondylolisthesis with foraminal stenosis; or corpectomy removing at least one-third of vertebral body).

Imaging findings include specific criteria for Adult Symptomatic Degenerative Spinal Deformity (e.g., Cobb angle >30°, asymmetric disk collapse, global coronal imbalance, sagittal vertebral axis >8cm, or pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis >15°).

Imaging findings include specific criteria for Initial Disc Herniation (e.g., extraforaminal L5-S1 herniation where far lateral approach is not feasible; foraminal herniation requiring facet resection; or herniation at level of spinal cord/conus medullaris).
Imaging findings include specific criteria for Recurrent Disc Herniation (evidence of anterolisthesis with dynamic instability >3mm or Meyerding Grade II+).

Documentation of nicotine-free status: individual is a never-smoker OR has refrained from smoking, smokeless tobacco, and nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery, validated by objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) within normal range.
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.4: Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) with Decompression (Indirect or Direct) (TOC: S7.1)

Required findings: Imaging findings for Degenerative Spondylolisthesis without Spondylolysis: dynamic segmental instability >3mm on flexion-extension/supine-upright x-rays OR Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis.

Imaging findings for Spondylolisthesis with Spondylolysis: Meyerding Grade I/II with progression, Grade III+ with ≥50% slippage or progression, progressive pain without confirmatory imaging of progression, or multi-level spondylolysis.
Imaging findings for Discogenic Lower Back Pain/Degenerative Disc Disease: plain x-rays and advanced imaging (CT, MRI) show moderate to severe single-level disc degeneration.

Imaging findings for Adult Symptomatic Degenerative Spinal Deformity: coronal plane deformity (Cobb >30°, asymmetric disk collapse, global imbalance) OR sagittal imbalance (sagittal vertebral axis >8cm, pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis >15°).
Symptoms include significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing).

Less than clinically meaningful improvement with conservative management for at least three (3) consecutive months (for spondylolisthesis/deformity) or at least 12 consecutive months (for discogenic pain) with prescription analgesics/steroids/gabapentinoids/NSAIDs and/or provider-directed exercise program.

For Discogenic Lower Back Pain: Structured physician-supervised, multi-modal, nonoperative management including regularly scheduled appointments, follow-up evaluation, and less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following: prescription meds (12 months), exercise program (12 months), epidural steroid/nerve root blocks, or facet joint injections/RFA.
Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders).

Documentation of nicotine-free status: individual is a never-smoker OR has refrained from smoking, smokeless tobacco, and nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery, validated by objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) within normal range.
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.5: Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) without Decompression (TOC: S8.1)

Non-Indications: Lumbar fusion for adjacent segment disease where the prior adjacent-level lumbar fusion was performed less than 6 months prior.
Lumbar fusion where the individual has not met the specific clinical and imaging criteria for the applicable procedure-specific section (CMM-609.4 or CMM-609.5).

Lumbar fusion for Actual Instability where imaging does not demonstrate dynamic segmental instability (>3mm difference), Meyerding Grade II+ (for degenerative), or specific spondylolysis progression criteria, unless instability is created/identified intra-operatively.

Lumbar fusion for Anticipated Iatrogenic Instability where the anticipated instability does not meet specific thresholds (e.g., facet excision <50% bilateral and <75% single facet, or corpectomy <1/3 vertebral body).
Lumbar fusion for Recurrent Disc Herniation where imaging does not show anterolisthesis with dynamic instability (>3mm) or Meyerding Grade II+ spondylolisthesis.

Lumbar fusion for Discogenic Lower Back Pain where the duration of chronic, unremitting pain is less than one year, or where there has been clinically meaningful improvement with conservative management, or where the patient has not undergone structured multi-modal nonoperative management for the required duration (12 months for meds/exercise).

Lumbar fusion where the individual has unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders).

Lumbar fusion where the individual is a current smoker or has used smokeless tobacco/nicotine replacement therapy within the last six (6) weeks, or where objective cotinine testing is not within the normal range.
Important criteria & exceptions: Criteria exception for Actual Instability: When instability is created and/or identified intra-operatively, the pre-operative imaging criteria for instability are NOT required.

For Discogenic Lower Back Pain, the conservative management trial requires less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the specified modalities (meds, exercise, injections) for at least 12 consecutive months, which is longer than the 3-month requirement for other conditions.
Nicotine-free status must be validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the specific testing method and lab.
Documentation required: Documentation of the date of the prior adjacent-level lumbar fusion to verify the 6-month interval.

Imaging reports (plain x-rays, flexion-extension views, supine/upright comparisons, CT, MRI) demonstrating specific findings such as spondylolisthesis grade, dynamic instability measurements (>3mm), Cobb angles, sagittal vertebral axis, pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis, or disc degeneration severity.
Objective cotinine testing results (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range, or documentation of never-smoker status.

Records of conservative management including prescription medication history, provider-directed exercise program records (prescribed by PT, chiropractor, or physician), and records of epidural steroid injections, selective nerve root blocks, facet joint injections, or radiofrequency ablations.
Documentation of the absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders.
Clinical notes documenting significant daily pain and clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing).
